docs.title: CMBLensing.py
docs.text:
CMBLensing.py is the JAX port of the Julia package CMBLensing.jl. It

  • simulates flat-sky CMB temperature and polarization fields, lensing potentials and noisy lensed data maps (load_sim),
  • lenses, inverse-lenses and adjoint-lenses fields with the LenseFlow ODE (lense_flow),
  • reconstructs the unlensed field and the lensing potential by joint MAP optimization (map_joint),
  • samples the LCDM parameters jointly with the field and the lensing potential by Gibbs sampling (sample_joint), extending the algorithm developed by Millea et al. 2020,
  • forecasts the sampler's posterior widths with a Gaussian Fisher forecast (fisher_forecast).

All array operations run in JAX (float64), so the code runs on CPU and GPU and is differentiable where it needs to be.

docs.title: Fisher Forecast
docs.text:
A Gaussian Fisher forecast of the sampler's posterior widths, from two covariance blocks on the sampler's own rfft grid:

Block Covariance delensed T \(C_{TT}^\text{delensed} + C_n\) (\(C_n\) analytic, theta independent) phi \(C_\phi + N_\phi\) (\(N_\phi\) frozen at \(\theta_0\)) \[ F_{ij} = \frac{1}{2} \sum_\text{blocks} \sum_k w_k \, \frac{\partial \ln C_k}{\partial \theta_i} \frac{\partial \ln C_k}{\partial \theta_j}, \]

with \(w_k\) the rfft mode weights (2 per bulk mode, 1 on the self-conjugate columns) and central finite differences of step \(h = 0.05\,\sigma\) from direct CAMB calls.

docs.title: One N_phi drives both blocks
docs.text:
N_phi is the phi block's noise and also sets the residual lensing in the delensed T through \(A_L = N_L / (C_L + N_L)\). --nphi_source picks it:

--nphi_source N_phi Role qe_unlensed box QE with the unlensed C_TT in its filter upper bound on the information qe_delensed (default) box QE with the filter iterated to the delensed C_TT lower bound map_joint nphi of map_joint_phi_noise.npz (--phi_noise) comparison sample_joint nphi of sampler_phi_noise.npz (--phi_noise) comparison

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
python -m cmb_lensing.fisher_forecast --noise 5 --nphi_source qe_unlensed                       #upper bound
python -m cmb_lensing.fisher_forecast --noise 5 --nphi_source qe_delensed --qe_response gradient #lower bound
python -m cmb_lensing.fisher_forecast --noise 5 --nphi_source map_joint --phi_noise map_joint_phi_noise.npz
python -m cmb_lensing.fisher_forecast --noise 5 --nphi_source sample_joint --phi_noise sampler_phi_noise.npz
python -m cmb_lensing.fisher_forecast --noise 5 --nphi_source qe_unlensed --delensed_covariance delensed_covariance.npz

Other flags: --nside, --theta_pix, --l_knee, --beam_fwhm, --params (default logA omch2 theta_MC_100), --camb_lmax, --stability (also computes at step 2h).

By default the T block is CAMB's partially delensed spectrum at the frozen \(A_L\). --delensed_covariance swaps in the empirical delensed covariance.

Outputs go to cmb_lensing/fisher_output/fisher*_from_blocks_<nphi>_<camb|empirical>_<noise>_uk.*, with parameters in the order omch2, ombh2, ns, theta_MC_100, logA.

The load_sim() method from the simulate sub-module allows the user to generate a data_set object which contains unlensed CMB temperature and polarization fields, the corresponding lensed fields, the lensing potential, "data" fields which represent the lensed fields with a mask and beam applied along with instrumental noise, and all the other covariance matrices and operators that will be necessary for CMB Lensing and field estimation.

                    theta_pix = 2, #Arcminutes per pixel
                    pol = "IP", #Specify IP for temperature and E + B Modes, I for temp only, or P for E + B only
                    master_seed = 67, #Specify a seed for reproduceable results
                    r = 0.2, nt = -0.025, k_pivot = 0.002,
                    max_l_tensor = 8_000,
                    max_eta_k_tensor = 16_000,
                    uk_arcmin_t = 3) #Noise level in data fields

In order to converge on accurately estimated lensing potentials and CMB fields, we need an objective function to minimize. The CMBLensing.py package does this by taking gradients of the logpdf function which takes the following mathematical form:

\[-2*\mathrm{logpdf} = \frac{(\mathrm{data} - M * B * L * f)^2}{C_n} + \frac{f^2}{C_f} + \frac{\phi^2}{C_{\phi}} + \mathrm{logdet}(C_{\phi}) + \mathrm{logdet}(C_f) + \mathrm{logdet}(C_n)\]

We begin by running a simulation to generate the ground truth data field at the fiducial LCDM cosmology. We set the noise level to \(5 \mu\) K-arcmin, resolution to \(\theta_\mathrm{pix} = 2.5\) arcminutes per pixel, and look at a single \(64 \times 64\) pixel temperature map. The lmax flag determine the max multipole we run CAMB out to. Past this value, the power spectra are found via log-interpolation.

In [2]: Copied! 
#generate a data set with the LCDM parameters held at ground truth
ground_truth_params = load_sim_cosmology(GROUND_TRUTH)
noise_level = 5
data_set = load_sim(nside = 64, theta_pix = 2.5, pol = "I", 
                    master_seed = 42, uk_arcmin_t = noise_level,
                    **ground_truth_params, r = 0, 
                    nt = 0, lmax = 4000)
#generate a data set with the LCDM parameters held at ground truth ground_truth_params = load_sim_cosmology(GROUND_TRUTH) noise_level = 5 data_set = load_sim(nside = 64, theta_pix = 2.5, pol = "I", master_seed = 42, uk_arcmin_t = noise_level, **ground_truth_params, r = 0, nt = 0, lmax = 4000)

Now we run the sample_joint algorithm which takes the data_set as input and outputs samples of the cosmological parameters. Here we only want to look at samples of the single parameter logA, but the current state of sample_joint allows for joint sampling of 5 of the 6 LCDM parameters (we take a prior value on the optical depth to reionization \(\tau_\mathrm{reio} = 0.05\)). In general, the more parameters one wants to jointly sample, the stronger the degeneracies between individual parameters become, and we must move to larger and larger map sizes and finer resolutions in order to obtain meaningful samples. The first time you run the following cell, the ~7.9 GB camb_grid_spline.npz file is downloaded automatically from Hugging Face into the camb_splines/ directory (see the installation page for more on this), so expect a wait.

Below we plot the trace of the logA samples differenced with respect to the ground truth value and normalizaed relative to the sigma of the search range for this parameter. We see that there is an initial burn-in as we start far away from the typical set. Then around the 200 point mark, we start sampling from the true distribution of logA and the normalized samples scatter equally within 1 sigma of the ground truth. We can also plot the log(PDF) value of the distribution function we are sampling from. We see that it started to plateau even quicker than the logA trace plot did. The story here is essentially the same: we start at a point in parameter space far away from the ground truth, then slowly burn-in and start sampling from the true logA distribution. Notice that we do not stay fixed on the ground truth value and instead oscillate around it. This is to be expected. Our goal here is to learn the distribution of logA, not necessarily the exact ground truth value. The average scatter of the samples is our way of determining how confident we are in the learned mean. High scatter indicates low confidence and vice versa.

In general, thinning your samples widens your learned distribution, so the kernel density estimate we present here is overconfident relative to what it really should be.

Now below we plot the autocorrelation function in terms of lag. This tells us how correlated two samples are for points separated by a certain distance. We can then integrate the autocorrelation function to get a single number - the Integrated Autocorrelation Time - which represents how many samples it takes for two points to become completely decorrelated. In our case, this number turns out to be very small, only around \(\sim 4\).

In [7]: Copied! 
#-------- Autocorrelation Function ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def autocorrelation(chain, max_lag = None):
    """Normalized autocorrelation of a 1D chain of samples."""
    n = len(chain)
    if max_lag is None:
        max_lag = n // 2
    x = chain - np.mean(chain)
    variance = np.var(chain)
    acf = np.correlate(x, x, mode = "full")[n - 1:]  #positive lags only
    acf = acf[:max_lag] / (variance * n)
    return acf

#-------- Integrated Autocorrelation Time -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
def integrated_autocorrelation_time(acf, c = 5.0):
    """Sokal's automatic windowing — truncate at lag M where M < c * tau(M)."""
    tau = 1.0
    for m in range(1, len(acf)):
        tau += 2.0 * acf[m]
        if m >= c * tau:
            return tau
    return tau

acf = autocorrelation(burnt_samples)
iat = np.ceil(integrated_autocorrelation_time(acf))
plt.figure(figsize = (8, 5))

plt.axhline(0, color = "black", label = "Zero Line")

plt.xlabel("Lag")

Here we have drawn samples from a single parameter from a single chain run on a single data map. In practice, one chain on one data map is not a statistically powerful statement due to MCMC noise and cosmic variance (especially on such a small map). The standard workflow is to run the sampling algorithm on multiple different data map realizations at the ground truth cosmology (order 10 - 100 map realizations). For each data map realization when then typically run 5 - 10 sub-chains where we initialize the LCDM parameters to random values for each sub-chain. We then pool samples from the same data maps into a single KDE per map and take the map-wise product of these KDE's to get a single distribution that represents the best estimate we have given all the data for the parameter of interest. For those who are interested in using CMBLensing.py for LCDM parameter inference, the machinery to do big runs like this is laid out in the module get_lcdm_samples and described in more detail in the codebase's documentation.

@struct.dataclass
class DiagonalScalar(FieldOperator):
    """An operator diagonal in Fourier space acting on `FlatS0` fields (e.g. C_TT, C_phi).

    `operator * field` multiplies mode by mode. Operators also combine with each other and
    with scalars through +, - and *; `pinv` and `log_det` are defined for them.

    Attributes:
        scalar_matrix: The diagonal, an (nside, nside//2+1) array on the rfft2 grid.
        nside: Number of pixels on a side.
        theta_pix: Pixel width in arcmin.
        pix_width: Pixel width in radians.
        fourier_weights: Weight of each rfft2 mode.
    """

    scalar_matrix: jnp.ndarray = flax.struct.field(default_factory = lambda: FOURIER_MATRIX_DEFAULT.copy())

    def _matrix_names(self):
        return {"scalar_matrix"}

    #NOTE we must define operator-operator, operator-field, and operator scalar multiplication
    def __mul__(self, other):
        if isinstance(other, DiagonalScalar):
            return self.replace(scalar_matrix = self.scalar_matrix * other.scalar_matrix)
        elif isinstance(other, FlatS0):
            return other.replace(scalar_matrix = self.scalar_matrix * other.scalar_matrix)
        else:
            return self.replace(scalar_matrix = self.scalar_matrix * other)

    def __rmul__(self, other):
        return self.__mul__(other)

    independent B block.

    Products with another `BlockTEB` are matrix products of the T/E blocks, so they do not
    commute. `pinv` and `log_det` use Schur complements.

    Attributes:
        matrix_TT: TT block, an (nside, nside//2+1) array on the rfft2 grid.
        matrix_TE: TE block.
        matrix_ET: ET block.
        matrix_EE: EE block.
        matrix_BB: BB block.
        nside: Number of pixels on a side.
        theta_pix: Pixel width in arcmin.
        pix_width: Pixel width in radians.
        fourier_weights: Weight of each rfft2 mode.
    """

    #NOTE these matrices have the following 3 x 3 block diagonal format
    #[TT TE 0 ]
    #[ET EE 0 ]
    #[0  0  BB]

    matrix_TT: jnp.ndarray = flax.struct.field(default_factory = lambda: FOURIER_MATRIX_DEFAULT.copy())
    matrix_TE: jnp.ndarray = flax.struct.field(default_factory = lambda: FOURIER_MATRIX_DEFAULT.copy())
    matrix_ET: jnp.ndarray = flax.struct.field(default_factory = lambda: FOURIER_MATRIX_DEFAULT.copy())
    matrix_EE: jnp.ndarray = flax.struct.field(default_factory = lambda: FOURIER_MATRIX_DEFAULT.copy())
    matrix_BB: jnp.ndarray = flax.struct.field(default_factory = lambda: FOURIER_MATRIX_DEFAULT.copy())

    def _matrix_names(self):
        return {"matrix_TT", "matrix_TE", "matrix_ET", "matrix_EE", "matrix_BB"}

    #NOTE non-diagonal matrix multiplication is NOT commutative hence we need distinction
    #between multiplying on the left or right for BlockTEB matrices specifically
    def __mul__(self, other):

        #matrix-matrix multiplication, matrix-field multiplication, and matrix-scalar multiplication                                                                                                                                                               
        if isinstance(other, BlockTEB):
            #compute a non-diagonal matrix-matrix product                   
            return self.replace(matrix_TT = self.matrix_TT * other.matrix_TT + self.matrix_TE * other.matrix_ET,
                                matrix_ET = self.matrix_ET * other.matrix_TT + self.matrix_EE * other.matrix_ET,
                                matrix_TE = self.matrix_TT * other.matrix_TE + self.matrix_TE * other.matrix_EE,
                                matrix_EE = self.matrix_ET * other.matrix_TE + self.matrix_EE * other.matrix_EE,
                                matrix_BB = self.matrix_BB * other.matrix_BB)
        #matrix-field multiplication
        elif isinstance(other, FlatS02):
            return other.replace(scalar_matrix = self.matrix_TT * other.scalar_matrix + self.matrix_TE * other.polar_matrix_1,
                                 polar_matrix_1 = self.matrix_ET * other.scalar_matrix + self.matrix_EE * other.polar_matrix_1,
                                 polar_matrix_2 = self.matrix_BB * other.polar_matrix_2)
        #matrix-scalar multiplication
        return self.replace(matrix_TT = self.matrix_TT * other,
                            matrix_TE = self.matrix_TE * other,
                            matrix_ET = self.matrix_ET * other,
                            matrix_EE = self.matrix_EE * other,
                            matrix_BB = self.matrix_BB * other)                                                                                                                                         

    #NOTE we only expect to multiply a BlockTEB on the right by another BlockTEB or a scalar
    def __rmul__(self, other): 

        if isinstance(other, BlockTEB):
            #compute a non-diagonal matrix-matrix product                   
            return self.replace(matrix_TT = other.matrix_TT * self.matrix_TT + other.matrix_TE * self.matrix_ET,
                                matrix_ET = other.matrix_ET * self.matrix_TT + other.matrix_EE * self.matrix_ET,
                                matrix_TE = other.matrix_TT * self.matrix_TE + other.matrix_TE * self.matrix_EE,
                                matrix_EE = other.matrix_ET * self.matrix_TE + other.matrix_EE * self.matrix_EE,
                                matrix_BB = other.matrix_BB * self.matrix_BB)
        #matrix-scalar multiplication
        return self.replace(matrix_TT = self.matrix_TT * other,
                            matrix_TE = self.matrix_TE * other,
                            matrix_ET = self.matrix_ET * other,
                            matrix_EE = self.matrix_EE * other,
                            matrix_BB = self.matrix_BB * other)

def map_joint(data_set, num_steps = 30, constant_step = False):
    """Joint maximum a posteriori estimate of the unlensed field f and the lensing potential phi.

    Alternates a Wiener-filter step for f at the current phi with a step in phi along the
    preconditioned gradient of the mixed logpdf, the step length set by a BFGS line search.
    Starts from f = phi = 0. The cosmology is the one stored in the data set's covariances.

    Args:
        data_set: A `DataSetT`, `DataSetEB` or `DataSetTEB`, e.g. from `load_sim`.
        num_steps: Number of (f step, phi step) iterations.
        constant_step: If True, skip the line search and take unit-length phi steps.

    Returns:
        (f, phi): the estimated unlensed field (same type as `data_set.data`) and the
        estimated lensing potential (a `FlatS0`), both in Fourier space.

    Example:
        ```python
        from cmb_lensing.simulate import load_sim
        from cmb_lensing.map_joint import map_joint
        data_set = load_sim(nside = 64, theta_pix = 5, pol = "I", master_seed = 1)
        f_map, phi_map = map_joint(data_set)
        ```
    """

    #unpack the necessary data from the data set object
    noise_covariance = data_set.noise_covariance
    mixing_d = data_set.mixing_d
    #MAP joint method is invariant to G matrix so set to identity for simplicity here
    mixing_g = get_scalar_identity(mixing_d)
    field_covariance = data_set.field_covariance
    phi_covariance = data_set.phi_covariance
    quadratic_estimate = data_set.quadratic_estimate
    mask = data_set.mask
    beam = data_set.beam
    data = data_set.data

    #set starting guesses for f and phi to all zeros
    field_predict = 0*data #NOTE this is in general a TEB vector
    phi_predict = zero_scalar_field_like(data) #Phi only ever represents one singular field

    #compute the hessian which we will use to calculate the step in the phi direction 
    hessian = pinv(phi_gradient_hessian(phi_covariance, quadratic_estimate))
    alpha = jnp.array(1.0)
    for _ in range(num_steps):

        #compute the wiener filter of the predicted field
        field_predict = wiener_filter(field_predict, phi_predict, data, field_covariance, noise_covariance, mask, beam)

        #must mix f and phi before taking the gradient
        mixed_field, mixed_phi = mix(field_predict, phi_predict, mixing_d, mixing_g)
        mixed_grad_phi = mixed_grad_phi_logpdf(mixed_field, mixed_phi, data, noise_covariance, 
                                                phi_covariance, field_covariance, 
                                                mask, beam, mixing_d, mixing_g)

        #create a new partial function whose only input is alpha for use in the brent optimizer (we want to
        #minimize the value of this function w.r.t. the single parameter alpha)
        min_logpdf = partial(logpdf_at_phi_new, grad_phi = mixed_grad_phi, mixed_field = mixed_field, 
                             phi_predict = mixed_phi, data = data, beam = beam, mask = mask, field_covariance = field_covariance,
                             phi_covariance = phi_covariance, noise_covariance = noise_covariance,
                             mixing_d = mixing_d, mixing_g = mixing_g, hessian = hessian)

        if not constant_step:
            #call the optimizer to find which alpha minimizes the best
            optimizer = minimize(min_logpdf, 1, method = "BFGS") #Set a starting guess of "alpha = 1"
            alpha = optimizer.x[0]

        #take a step in the opposite direction of the gradient
        phi_predict = phi_predict + alpha * hessian * mixed_grad_phi

    #after max iterations have been looped through return the final learned fields
    return field_predict, phi_predict

    `USE_CAMB_GRID` / `USE_CAMB_SPLINE`.

    Args:
        data_set: The data, a `DataSetT`, `DataSetEB` or `DataSetTEB` (e.g. from
            `load_sim`). Its type sets the polarization mode.
        param_init: {name: value} starting point, all five parameters.
        proposal_sigmas: {name: width} of the Gaussian Metropolis proposal per parameter.
            The parameters are updated in this dict's order. Tune toward ~44 % acceptance.
        param_ranges: {name: (low, high)}; proposals outside the range are rejected.
        should_sample: {name: bool}; parameters set to False stay at `param_init`.
        noise_level: White noise level of the data in uK-arcmin.
        advanced_logging: {"phi_acceptance", "lcdm_acceptance", "plot_log_pdf",
            "plot_lcdm_sigmas": bool}. The first two print running acceptance rates, the
            last two overwrite progress plots in `cmb_lensing/sample_lcdm_output/` (which
            must exist) every iteration.
        fixed_fields: Debugging option: hold f and phi at the data set's true fields and
            sample theta only.
        phi_init: Starting phi: "MAP" (the `map_joint` estimate, default), "RNG" (a draw
            from the phi step's inverse mass matrix) or anything else for zero.
        hmc_num_steps: Leapfrog steps per phi HMC step.
        hmc_step_size: Leapfrog step size. Tune toward ~65 % phi acceptance.
        iters_per_chain: Number of Gibbs iterations.
        num_burn_in_fix_theta: Iterations before the parameters start to move.
        num_burn_in_always_accept: Iterations for which every phi HMC step is accepted.
        resume_chain_dict: Restart a saved chain: a dict with one entry per parameter name,
            "phi_map" and "sub_key" (e.g. `np.load` of the npz `run_single_lcdm_chain.py`
            writes). Overrides `param_init` and `phi_init`.
        seed: Seed of the chain's random numbers. None draws one at random.
        map_idx: Data-map index used in the history file names.
        sub_chain_idx: Chain index used in the history file names.
        lmax: Largest multipole of the spectra.
        metropolis_num_steps: Metropolis moves per parameter per iteration.
        hpc_path: If set, every iteration appends each sampled parameter's latest value to
            `{hpc_path}{name}_map_{map_idx}_chain_{sub_chain_idx}_history.txt`.
        reparameterize_lcdm: Make the Metropolis moves along the axes of
            theta' = rotation_matrix @ theta instead of along the parameters themselves.
            Requires the 5D grid.
        rotation_matrix: (N, N) rotation over the N sampled parameters, taken in
            `PARAM_ORDER`. Used only with `reparameterize_lcdm`.
        rotated_proposal_sigmas: {name: width} of the proposal along each rotated axis, in
            the order of the rotation's rows. Used only with `reparameterize_lcdm`.

    Returns:
        (param_vals, phi, sub_key): param_vals is a dict of per-parameter lists of the
        chain's values (starting with `param_init`), phi the final lensing potential and
        sub_key the final random key, which together with the last parameter values let a
        chain be resumed.
    """

    #polarization mode follows the dataset
    if isinstance(data_set, DataSetTEB):
        pol = "IP"
    elif isinstance(data_set, DataSetEB):
        pol = "P"
    elif isinstance(data_set, DataSetT):
        pol = "I"
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"sample_joint supports DataSetT (pol = 'I'), DataSetEB "
                         f"(pol = 'P') and DataSetTEB (pol = 'IP') datasets, got "
                         f"{type(data_set).__name__}")
    if pol != "I" and not USE_CAMB_GRID:
        raise ValueError(f"pol = '{pol}' requires USE_CAMB_GRID - the "
                         "1D CAMB caches have no EE/BB spectra")
    bb_is_zero = camb_grid_bb_is_zero() if USE_CAMB_GRID else True

    #if a resume_chain_dict is specified (e.g. np.load of the npz run_single_lcdm_chain.py
    #writes: one entry per parameter name, "phi_map" and "sub_key"), restart from its parameters
    if resume_chain_dict is not None:
        param_init = {}
        for name in PARAM_ORDER:
            param_init[name] = float(resume_chain_dict[name])

    #the sampled parameters, in PARAM_ORDER - this is the subspace the rotation acts on, so its
    #order is what fixes the meaning of each rotation_matrix column
    theta_log_names = [name for name in PARAM_ORDER if should_sample.get(name, False)]
    sampled_idx = np.array([PARAM_INDEX[name] for name in theta_log_names], dtype = np.int64)

    #optional reparametrization: the theta step becomes a set of 1-D Metropolis moves along the
    #axes of theta' = rotation_matrix @ theta instead of along the sampled PARAM_ORDER axes
    if reparameterize_lcdm:
        rotation, rotation_pinv, rotated_names = prepare_rotation(rotation_matrix,
                                                                  rotated_proposal_sigmas,
                                                                  theta_log_names)
        if not USE_CAMB_GRID:
            raise ValueError("reparameterize_lcdm = True requires USE_CAMB_GRID - a rotated "
                             "proposal moves several parameters at once and the 1D caches pin "
                             "every parameter but one")
    else:
        rotation, rotation_pinv, rotated_names = None, None, []

    #Determine whether to use a 1-D interpolator or a 5-D interpolator
    if USE_CAMB_GRID:
        predictors = get_camb_grid_predictors()
        start_tt = predictors.tt(jnp.array([[param_init[k] for k in PARAM_ORDER]]))
        if not bool(jnp.all(jnp.isfinite(start_tt))):
            raise ValueError(
                f"the starting parameters {dict((k, param_init[k]) for k in PARAM_ORDER)} "
                f"fall outside the 5D CAMB grid, so the initial covariances would be NaN. "
                f"Check that theta_MC_100 is reachable at this ombh2/omch2 - see "
                f"theta_grid in {CAMB_GRID_PATH}")
    elif USE_CAMB_SPLINE:
        sampled_names = [name for name in PARAM_ORDER if should_sample.get(name, False)]
        if len(sampled_names) != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"USE_CAMB_SPLINE requires exactly one sampled parameter "
                             f"(the caches are 1D), got {sampled_names}")
        predictors = wrap_temp_predictors(*get_camb_spline_predictors(sampled_names[0]))
    else:
        raise ValueError("One of either USE_CAMB_GRID or USE_CAMB_SPLINE must be set to True")

    #Set the initial parameter values to the user specified starting guesses
    param_vals = {}
    for theta, theta_val in param_init.items():
        param_vals[theta] = [theta_val]
    #Also store the current parameter values in a JAX array
    current_params = jnp.array([param_init[k] for k in PARAM_ORDER], dtype = jnp.float64)

    #the rotated step works on plain numpy vectors over the SAMPLED subspace: theta_vec in the
    #original parameters and its image theta_vec_prime under the rotation, kept in step from here on
    theta_vec = np.array([param_init[k] for k in theta_log_names], dtype = np.float64)
    param_lo = np.array([float(param_ranges[k][0]) for k in theta_log_names], dtype = np.float64)
    param_hi = np.array([float(param_ranges[k][-1]) for k in theta_log_names], dtype = np.float64)
    theta_vec_prime = rotation @ theta_vec if reparameterize_lcdm else None

    #Add data that will be used throughout the sampling algorithm to an args dictionary
    args = {}
    args = add_metadata_to_args(args, data_set, lmax)
    args = add_starting_matrices_to_args(args, data_set, noise_level,
                                         param_init, current_params,
                                         predictors, pol = pol)

    #change data_set covariance matrices from ground truth to initial
    #starting point in cosmological parameter space
    data_set = set_initial_ds_conditions(data_set, args)
    data_field = data_set.data

    #Use a seed to get reproduceable results if so desired
    #otherwise use machine entropy to generate a random number
    if seed is not None:
        sub_key = jax.random.PRNGKey(seed)
    elif resume_chain_dict is not None:
        sub_key = jnp.asarray(resume_chain_dict["sub_key"])
    else:
        sub_key = jax.random.PRNGKey(np.random.randint(0, 2**31))

    #Setting the starting point in phi-space to be the MAP estimate (the mode) plus a random realization
    #of the Hessian pre-conditioner empirically seems to decrease the burn-in time (DEFAULT).
    #A resumed chain starts from its saved phi whatever phi_init says
    if resume_chain_dict is not None:
        phi = data_set.phi.replace(scalar_matrix = jnp.asarray(resume_chain_dict["phi_map"]))
    elif phi_init == "MAP":
        _, phi_map = map_joint(data_set)
        phi = phi_map
    elif phi_init == "RNG":
        inv_mass_matrix = pinv(pinv(args["phi_covariance"]) + pinv(args["quadratic_estimate"]))
        rng_key, sub_key = jax.random.split(sub_key)
        phi_rng_matrix = field_from_covar_single_key(data_set.data.nside, inv_mass_matrix.scalar_matrix, rng_key)
        phi = data_set.phi.replace(scalar_matrix = jfft.rfft2(phi_rng_matrix))
    else:
        phi = 0*data_set.phi

    #We repeatedly draw a fresh temperature / polarization field, so we need a "zeroes" object
    #of the same class as the temperature / polarization field
    field_zeroes = 0*data_set.unlensed_field

    #the stacked data matrices handed to every jitted theta kernel
    data_stack = field_matrix_stack(data_field, pol)

    #lists used to track sampling acceptance rates
    phi_acceptance = []
    mixed_logpdf_values = []
    lcdm_acceptance = {}
    lcdm_acceptance["theta_MC_100"] = []
    lcdm_acceptance["ombh2"] = []
    lcdm_acceptance["omch2"] = []
    lcdm_acceptance["ns"] = []
    lcdm_acceptance["logA"] = []
    for rotated_name in rotated_names:
        lcdm_acceptance[rotated_name] = []

    for iter in range(1, iters_per_chain + 1):

        #The "fixed_fields" flag can be used for quick debugging of the theta step 
        #assuming we have perfect knowledge of the ground truth (f, phi) pair
        if not fixed_fields:
            #1. sample the temperature field
            rng_key, sub_key = jax.random.split(sub_key)
            temp_field = gibbs_sample_f(field_zeroes, data_field, phi, args, rng_key)

            #2. mix the fields
            mixed_temp, mixed_phi = mix(temp_field, phi, args["mixing_d"], args["mixing_g"])

            #3. sample the lensing potential phi
            rng_key, sub_key = jax.random.split(sub_key)
            mixed_phi, delta_h, accept = gibbs_sample_phi(mixed_phi, mixed_temp, data_field, rng_key,
                                                          args, iter, num_burn_in_always_accept,
                                                          hmc_num_steps = hmc_num_steps, 
                                                          hmc_step_size = hmc_step_size)
            if advanced_logging["phi_acceptance"]:
                phi_acceptance.append(int(accept))
                print(f"Phi accept rate = {np.sum(np.array(phi_acceptance)) / len(phi_acceptance)}")
                print(f"delta_H = {delta_h}")
        else:
            mixed_temp, mixed_phi = mix(data_set.unlensed_field, data_set.phi, 
                                        args["mixing_d"], args["mixing_g"])

        #4. sample your cosmo parameters
        if iter >= num_burn_in_fix_theta:
            if reparameterize_lcdm:
                #a sweep of 1-D Metropolis moves, one per axis of the rotated parametrization
                for rotated_idx, rotated_name in enumerate(rotated_names):
                    rng_key, sub_key = jax.random.split(sub_key)
                    theta_vec, theta_vec_prime = gibbs_sample_rotated_theta(
                                                   rotated_name, rotated_idx,
                                                   theta_vec, theta_vec_prime,
                                                   rotation, rotation_pinv, param_lo, param_hi,
                                                   sampled_idx,
                                                   lcdm_acceptance, advanced_logging["lcdm_acceptance"],
                                                   field_matrix_stack(mixed_temp, pol),
                                                   mixed_phi.scalar_matrix, data_stack,
                                                   current_params, rng_key,
                                                   args["nside"], args["pix_width"], data_field.theta_pix,
                                                   args["ell_grid"],
                                                   args["quadratic_estimate"].scalar_matrix,
                                                   op_matrix_stack(args["noise_covariance"], pol),
                                                   op_shared_matrix(args["mask"], pol),
                                                   op_shared_matrix(args["beam"], pol),
                                                   data_field.fourier_weights,
                                                   proposal_sigma = rotated_proposal_sigmas[rotated_name],
                                                   metropolis_num_steps = metropolis_num_steps,
                                                   pol = pol, bb_is_zero = bb_is_zero)

                    #the next axis of the sweep conditions on the position this one left behind
                    current_params = current_params.at[jnp.asarray(sampled_idx)].set(
                                        jnp.asarray(theta_vec, dtype = jnp.float64))

                #a rotated move generally changes every sampled parameter, so all of them are recorded
                for i, name in enumerate(theta_log_names):
                    param_vals[name].append(np.asarray(theta_vec[i], dtype = np.float64))

            for theta, proposal_sigma in list(proposal_sigmas.items()):
                if should_sample[theta] and not reparameterize_lcdm:
                    rng_key, sub_key = jax.random.split(sub_key)
                    theta_key_idx = PARAM_INDEX[theta]
                    theta_val = gibbs_sample_theta(jnp.array(theta_key_idx), param_ranges[theta], 
                                                   jnp.array(param_vals[theta][-1]),
                                                   lcdm_acceptance, advanced_logging["lcdm_acceptance"],
                                                   field_matrix_stack(mixed_temp, pol),
                                                   mixed_phi.scalar_matrix, data_stack,
                                                   current_params, rng_key, 
                                                   args["nside"], args["pix_width"], data_field.theta_pix,
                                                   args["ell_grid"],
                                                   args["quadratic_estimate"].scalar_matrix,
                                                   op_matrix_stack(args["noise_covariance"], pol),
                                                   op_shared_matrix(args["mask"], pol), 
                                                   op_shared_matrix(args["beam"], pol),
                                                   data_field.fourier_weights,
                                                   proposal_sigma = proposal_sigma,
                                                   metropolis_num_steps = metropolis_num_steps,
                                                   pol = pol, bb_is_zero = bb_is_zero)
                    param_vals[theta].append(theta_val)
                    current_params = current_params.at[theta_key_idx].set(theta_val)

            #5. recompute mixing and covariance matrices using the newly sampled parameter values
            args = update_args_after_sample(current_params, predictors, args, pol = pol)

        #6. unmix the fields using the updated version of the G & D matrices
        if not fixed_fields:
            _, phi = unmix(mixed_temp, mixed_phi, args["mixing_d"], args["mixing_g"])

        #7. plot certain diagnostics if user specified
        if advanced_logging["plot_log_pdf"]:
            mixed_logpdf_value = mixed_logpdf(mixed_temp, mixed_phi, data_field, args["noise_covariance"], 
                                              args["phi_covariance"], args["field_covariance"], 
                                              args["mask"], args["beam"], 
                                              args["mixing_g"], args["mixing_d"])
            mixed_logpdf_values.append(mixed_logpdf_value)
            plt.figure(figsize = (16, 10))
            plt.plot(mixed_logpdf_values, marker = "o")
            plt.title("Mixed LogPDF Over Time")
            plt.xlabel("Iteration")
            plt.ylabel("Mixed LogPDF Value")
            plt.legend()
            path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
                                "cmb_lensing", "sample_lcdm_output", "logpdf_progress.png")
            plt.savefig(path)
            plt.close() 

        if advanced_logging["plot_lcdm_sigmas"]:
            plt.figure(figsize = (16, 10))
            for name in theta_log_names:
                normalized = (np.array(param_vals[name]) - GROUND_TRUTH[name]) / PARAM_SIGMA[name]
                plt.plot(normalized, label = name, marker = "o")
            plt.axhline(0, color = "black", label = "Zero Sigma")
            plt.axhline(1, color = "grey", label = "+/- 1 Sigma")
            plt.axhline(-1, color = "grey")
            plt.title("(mean - sample)/sigma")
            plt.xlabel("Iteration")
            plt.ylabel("Standard Deviations")
            plt.legend()
            path = os.path.join(os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))),
                                "cmb_lensing", "sample_lcdm_output", "lcdm_progress.png")
            plt.savefig(path)
            plt.close()

        #Log chains to .txt files if we are running a larger experiment on an HPC
        if hpc_path is not None:
            for theta in theta_log_names:
                theta_path = hpc_path + f"{theta}_map_{map_idx}_chain_{sub_chain_idx}_history.txt"
                with open(theta_path, "a") as file:
                    file.write(str(param_vals[theta][-1]) + "\n")

    return param_vals, phi, sub_key

def load_sim(nside, theta_pix, pol, master_seed, uk_arcmin_t = 3, H0 = None,
             ombh2 = 0.0224567, omch2 = 0.118489, cosmomc_theta = 0.0104098,
             r = 0.0, mnu = DEFAULT_MNU, tau = DEFAULT_TAUREIO, As = jnp.exp(3.043) * 1e-10,
             nt = 0, ns = 0.968602, lmax = 4000, begin_ell_interp = None, l_knee = 100,
             k_pivot = DEFAULT_K_PIVOT, Alens = DEFAULT_A_LENSE, nphi_fac = 2, a_phi = 1,
             precomputed_cls = None, max_l_tensor = DEFAULT_MAX_L_TENSOR,
             max_eta_k_tensor = DEFAULT_MAX_ETA_K_TENSOR, use_mask = False):
    """Simulate a lensed CMB data set on a flat nside x nside sky patch.

    Runs CAMB for the requested cosmology, builds the field, phi and noise covariances in
    Fourier space, draws the unlensed field(s), phi and the noise, lenses the field with
    LenseFlow and returns everything in one data set object. CAMB runs inside
    `jax.pure_callback`, so a CAMB failure gives NaN spectra rather than an exception.

    Randomness: one root key PRNGKey(master_seed), and every random field (phi, then the
    unlensed field(s), then the noise) splits its own subkey off it in that fixed order
    (field_from_covar). So the realization at a seed depends on the cosmology only through
    the covariances the white noise is scaled by.

    Args:
        nside: Number of pixels on a side.
        theta_pix: Pixel width in arcmin.
        pol: "I" (temperature only), "P" (E/B polarization only) or "IP" (both).
        master_seed: Root seed of every random draw.
        uk_arcmin_t: White noise level in temperature, in uK-arcmin. The polarization
            noise is sqrt(2) higher.
        H0: Hubble constant. Leave as None to set the expansion through `cosmomc_theta`.
        ombh2: Physical baryon density.
        omch2: Physical cold dark matter density.
        cosmomc_theta: CosmoMC's approximation to the angular size of the sound horizon
            (the sampler's theta_MC_100 divided by 100).
        r: Tensor-to-scalar ratio.
        mnu: Sum of the neutrino masses in eV.
        tau: Optical depth to reionization.
        As: Primordial scalar amplitude (the sampler's logA is log(1e10 As)).
        nt: Tensor spectral index.
        ns: Scalar spectral index.
        lmax: Largest multipole of the spectra.
        begin_ell_interp: Optional multipole past which the spectra are extrapolated
            rather than taken from CAMB.
        l_knee: Knee of the 1/f noise term. 0 gives pure white noise, as every sampler
            entry point uses.
        k_pivot: Pivot scale of the primordial spectra, in 1/Mpc.
        Alens: CAMB's lensing amplitude.
        nphi_fac: Factor the quadratic-estimate noise is divided by (CMBLensing.jl's
            preconditioning heuristic).
        a_phi: Amplitude multiplying the phi covariance.
        precomputed_cls: Optional dict of CAMB spectra to use instead of running CAMB, for
            callers that build many realizations at one cosmology. It must be in
            `_extract_all_cls`'s format (e.g. the output of
            `fisher_forecast.camb_cls_at_params`) and must belong to the same cosmology as
            the keyword arguments, which are then unused.
        max_l_tensor: CAMB's largest multipole for the tensor spectra.
        max_eta_k_tensor: CAMB's largest k * eta for the tensor spectra.
        use_mask: Apply a sky mask. False (the default) uses a mask of all ones.

    Returns:
        A `DataSetT` (pol = "I"), `DataSetEB` (pol = "P") or `DataSetTEB` (pol = "IP")
        holding the fields (`unlensed_field`, `lensed_field`, `phi`, `data`) and the
        operators (`field_covariance`, `phi_covariance`, `noise_covariance`, `mask`,
        `beam`, `mixing_d`, `mixing_g`, `quadratic_estimate`, ...). All fields are in
        Fourier space.

    Example:
        ```python
        from cmb_lensing.simulate import load_sim
        data_set = load_sim(nside = 128, theta_pix = 2.5, pol = "IP", master_seed = 67,
                            uk_arcmin_t = 5, l_knee = 0)
        ```
    """

    lmax_prime = min(lmax, DEFAULT_MAX_ELL) if begin_ell_interp is None else min(lmax, begin_ell_interp)

    if precomputed_cls is None:
        unlensed_scalar, tensor, total, lens_potential = _camb_via_callback(
            H0, ombh2, omch2, cosmomc_theta, r, mnu, tau, As, nt, ns,
            lmax_prime, k_pivot, Alens, max_l_tensor, max_eta_k_tensor
        )
        cls = _extract_all_cls(unlensed_scalar, tensor, total, lens_potential, lmax, lmax_prime)
    else:
        cls = _validate_precomputed_cls(precomputed_cls, lmax)

    ell_grid, pix_width = gen_ell_grid(nside, theta_pix)
    #one root key; every draw below splits its own subkey off it (field_from_covar). The draw
    #ORDER (phi, the field(s), the noise) is fixed and independent of the cosmology, so two
    #calls at the same seed share every white-noise realization - the common random numbers
    #delensed_covariance.py's stencil relies on
    rng_key = jax.random.PRNGKey(master_seed)
    ells = jnp.arange(2, lmax).astype(jnp.float64)

    #ells arrays matched to the cls lengths: the emulator override returns ells
    #2..lmax inclusive while the CAMB dl2cl path returns 2..lmax-1
    phi_ells = jnp.arange(2, 2 + cls["phi"].shape[0]).astype(jnp.float64)

    #Lensing potential
    unscaled_cphi = covar_matrix_from_cls(nside, pix_width, ell_grid,
                                          phi_ells,
                                          cls["phi"], origin_value=0)
    cphi = a_phi * unscaled_cphi
    phi, rng_key = field_from_covar(nside, cphi, rng_key)

    #Unlensed field covariances (scalar + tensor). Unlensed scalar BB (identically zero
    #at r = 0) cannot go through the log-interpolating covariance builder (log(0) -> NaN)
    #so _covar_or_zeros maps it to an exactly zero matrix. TE crosses zero, so it is
    #built from the correlation ratio rho = Cl_TE / sqrt(Cl_TT * Cl_EE) instead
    #(te_covar_from_rho): linear interpolation of rho onto the ell grid, scaled by
    #sqrt(cf_tt * cf_ee), which keeps the T/E block positive semi-definite by
    #construction and matched to the sampler's grid-spline TE path
    cf = {}
    cf_scalar = {}
    cf_tensor = {}
    pol_comps = ("TT",) if pol == "I" else ("TT", "EE", "BB")
    for comp in pol_comps:
        scalar_ells = jnp.arange(2, 2 + cls[f"scalar_{comp}"].shape[0]).astype(jnp.float64)
        cf_scalar[comp] = _covar_or_zeros(nside, pix_width, ell_grid,
                                          scalar_ells,
                                          cls[f"scalar_{comp}"], origin_value=0)
        cf_tensor[comp] = _covar_or_zeros(nside, pix_width, ell_grid, ells,
                                          cls[f"tensor_{comp}"], origin_value=0)
        cf[comp] = cf_scalar[comp] + cf_tensor[comp]
    if pol != "I":
        scalar_ells = jnp.arange(2, 2 + cls["scalar_TE"].shape[0]).astype(jnp.float64)
        rho_te = te_rho_from_cls(cls["scalar_TE"], cls["scalar_TT"], cls["scalar_EE"])
        cf["TE"] = cf_scalar["TE"] = te_covar_from_rho(rho_te, scalar_ells, ell_grid,
                                                       cf["TT"], cf["EE"])
        cf_tensor["TE"] = jnp.zeros((nside, nside // 2 + 1))

    #Lensed field covariances (TE via the same correlation-ratio route)
    cfl = {comp: covar_matrix_from_cls(nside, pix_width, ell_grid, ells,
                                       cls[f"total_{comp}"], origin_value=0)
           for comp in ("TT", "EE", "BB")}
    rho_te_lensed = te_rho_from_cls(cls["total_TE"], cls["total_TT"], cls["total_EE"])
    cfl["TE"] = te_covar_from_rho(rho_te_lensed, ells, ell_grid, cfl["TT"], cfl["EE"])

    #Unlensed random fields. T and E are drawn CORRELATED to match the model's TE block:
    #E ~ N(0, C_EE), then T = (C_TE / C_EE) E + t_indep with
    #t_indep ~ N(0, C_TT - C_TE^2 / C_EE), which gives exactly
    #Cov = [[C_TT, C_TE], [C_TE, C_EE]] (the conditional variance is
    #C_TT (1 - rho^2) >= 0 by the |rho| <= 1 construction; the maximum(0) guards
    #round-off only). The B draw against a zero covariance gives an exactly zero field
    if pol == "I":
        field_t, rng_key = field_from_covar(nside, cf["TT"], rng_key)
    else:
        conditional_tt = jnp.maximum(
            cf["TT"] - cf["TE"]**2 * reciprocal_matrix(cf["EE"]), 0.0)
        t_indep, rng_key = field_from_covar(nside, conditional_tt, rng_key)
        field_e, rng_key = field_from_covar(nside, cf["EE"], rng_key)
        field_b, rng_key = field_from_covar(nside, cf["BB"], rng_key)
        te_ratio = cf["TE"] * reciprocal_matrix(cf["EE"])
        field_t = jfft.irfft2(te_ratio * jfft.rfft2(field_e)) + t_indep

    #Lensing
    if pol == "I":
        lensed_t = jfft.rfft2(primal_lense_flow(
            field_t, phi, pix_width, n=10, direction=FORWARD_LENSE, adjoint=False
        ))
    else:
        lensed_t, lensed_e, lensed_b = _lens_fields(
            field_t, field_e, field_b, phi, pix_width, nside, theta_pix
        )

    beam = get_beam(nside, pix_width, ell_grid, lmax_prime)
    #NOTE we have removed the mask for LCDM inference
    mask = get_mask(DEFAULT_MASK_ELL, nside, pix_width, ell_grid) if use_mask else jnp.ones_like(beam)

    #Noise covariance and white noise (the TE noise Cls are identically zero, so
    #_covar_or_zeros keeps that block an exact zero matrix instead of NaN)
    n_tt, n_te, n_ee, n_bb = noise_cls(lmax_prime, uk_arcmin_t, l_knee = l_knee)
    ell_prime = jnp.arange(2, lmax_prime)
    cn = {}
    for comp, ncl in zip(("TT", "TE", "EE", "BB"), (n_tt, n_te, n_ee, n_bb)):
        cn[comp] = _covar_or_zeros(nside, pix_width, ell_grid, ell_prime, ncl, origin_value=0)

    wn_t, rng_key = field_from_covar(nside, cn["TT"], rng_key)
    if pol != "I":
        wn_e, rng_key = field_from_covar(nside, cn["EE"], rng_key)
        wn_b, rng_key = field_from_covar(nside, cn["BB"], rng_key)

    #Data = Mask * Beam * Lensed + Noise
    data_t = mask * beam * lensed_t + jfft.rfft2(wn_t)
    if pol != "I":
        data_e = mask * beam * lensed_e + jfft.rfft2(wn_e)
        data_b = mask * beam * lensed_b + jfft.rfft2(wn_b)

    #Convert unlensed fields to Fourier space
    field_t = jfft.rfft2(field_t)
    if pol != "I":
        field_e, field_b = jfft.rfft2(field_e), jfft.rfft2(field_b)

    #D matrix (full T/E block including TE; see get_d_teb_matrix for the identity B
    #block at r = 0)
    d_tt = get_d_tt_matrix(cf["TT"], cn["TT"])
    if pol != "I":
        d_tt, d_te, d_ee, d_bb = get_d_teb_matrix(cf["TT"], cf["TE"], cf["EE"], cf["BB"],
                                                  cn["TT"], cn["TE"], cn["EE"], cn["BB"])

    #Quadratic estimate
    if pol == "I":
        qe = scalar_quadratic_estimate(cn["TT"], cf["TT"], cfl["TT"],
                                       mask, beam, pix_width) / nphi_fac
    else:
        qe = polar_quadratic_estimate(cf["EE"], cf["BB"], cfl["EE"], cfl["BB"],
                                      cn["EE"], cn["BB"], mask, mask,
                                      beam, beam, pix_width) / nphi_fac

    #The G mixing matrix    
    g = get_g_matrix(cphi, qe, a_phi, a_phi = a_phi)

    #convert phi back to fourier space
    phi = jfft.rfft2(phi)
    #Build dataset for the requested polarization
    if pol == "I":
        return _build_dataset_t(
            nside, theta_pix, pix_width, cphi, unscaled_cphi, qe, phi,
            cf, cf_scalar, cf_tensor, cfl, cn, d_tt, g, mask, beam,
            field_t, lensed_t, data_t, r, a_phi
        )
    elif pol == "P":
        return _build_dataset_eb(
            nside, theta_pix, pix_width, cphi, unscaled_cphi, qe, phi,
            cf, cf_scalar, cf_tensor, cfl, cn, d_ee, d_bb, g, mask, beam,
            field_e, field_b, lensed_e, lensed_b, data_e, data_b, r, a_phi
        )
    else:
        return _build_dataset_teb(
            nside, theta_pix, pix_width, cphi, unscaled_cphi, qe, phi,
            cf, cf_scalar, cf_tensor, cfl, cn, d_tt, d_te, d_ee, d_bb, g, mask, beam,
            field_t, field_e, field_b,
            lensed_t, lensed_e, lensed_b,
            data_t, data_e, data_b, r, a_phi
        )

docs.title: Fields
docs.text:
Maps live on a flat, periodic nside x nside box with theta_pix arcminutes per pixel. Three field types (cmb_lensing/fields.py) cover the polarization modes:

Type Content Arrays FlatS0 a scalar map (e.g. temperature or lensing potential) scalar_matrix FlatS2 polarization (E/B - Modes or Q/U - Modes) polar_matrix_1, polar_matrix_2 FlatS02 temperature + polarization scalar_matrix, polar_matrix_1, polar_matrix_2

A field carries a basis: either MAP (real space, (nside, nside), float64) or FOURIER (the rfft2 half plane, (nside, nside//2 + 1) complex128). Polarization is implicitly in either the EB or the QU parametrization. The conversions are

field = map(field)        #FOURIER -> MAP (irfft2)
field = fourier(field)    #MAP -> FOURIER (rfft2)
field = eb2qu(field)      #EB -> QU (in Fourier)
field = qu2eb(field)      #QU -> EB (in Fourier)

lense_flow takes fields in MAP / QU. Most other code works in FOURIER / EB.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
Diagonal-in-Fourier operators (covariances, beam, mask, the mixing matrices) are in cmb_lensing/matrix_operators.py:

Type Used for DiagonalScalar T-only, and every phi operator DiagonalEB E/B operators BlockTEB T/E/B operators with a 2x2 T/E block (TT, TE, ET, EE, BB)

Arithmetic is element-wise per block, except BlockTEB multiplication, which is the 2x2 T/E matrix product. pinv and log_det dispatch on the operator type.

Fields and operators are flax.struct.dataclass pytrees, so they pass through jax.jit, jax.grad and jax.vmap directly.

docs.title: Polarization modes
docs.text:
pol selects the configuration everywhere (load_sim, map_joint, sample_joint):

pol Fields Operators Data set "I" FlatS0 DiagonalScalar DataSetT "P" FlatS2 DiagonalEB DataSetEB "IP" FlatS02 BlockTEB DataSetTEB

docs.title: Simulating Data
docs.text:
cmb_lensing.simulate.load_sim is the main entry point. It

  1. runs CAMB for the requested cosmology,
  2. builds the field, phi and noise covariances in Fourier space,
  3. draws the unlensed field, phi and the noise,
  4. lenses the field with primal_lense_flow,
  5. returns a DataSetT / DataSetEB / DataSetTEB holding the fields, the operators and the simulated data.
from cmb_lensing.simulate import load_sim
data_set = load_sim(nside = 128,         #pixels per side
                    theta_pix = 2.5,     #arcmin per pixel
                    pol = "IP",          #"I", "P" or "IP"
                    master_seed = 67,
                    uk_arcmin_t = 5,     #white noise level in T (P is sqrt(2) higher)
                    l_knee = 0)          #0 for pure white noise

Useful attributes of the returned data set: unlensed_field, lensed_field, phi, data, field_covariance, phi_covariance, noise_covariance, mask, beam, mixing_d, mixing_g, quadratic_estimate.

docs.title: Choices to know about
docs.text:
• Noise sprectra are computed via noise_cls(...) with a 1/f term. The defaults are l_knee = 100 and alpha_knee = 3. The default beam FWHM is 0.
  • Cosmology is given in CAMB's names (cosmomc_theta, As, ombh2, omch2, ns, ...). The sampler's names (theta_MC_100, logA) are converted by to_camb_naming_conv (which edits its dict in place) or fisher_forecast.load_sim_cosmology.
  • CAMB runs inside jax.pure_callback, so load_sim is traceable. A CAMB failure gives NaN spectra and a non-finite logpdf, never an exception.

docs.title: MAP Estimation
docs.text:
map_joint(data_set, num_steps = 30, constant_step = False) (cmb_lensing/map_joint.py) finds the joint maximum a posteriori (f, phi) given the data, following Millea et al. 2017. The objective is

\[ -2 \log P(f, \phi \mid d) = \frac{(d - M B L(\phi) f)^2}{C_n} + \frac{f^2}{C_f} + \frac{\phi^2}{C_\phi} + \text{const.} \]

Each step alternates

  1. a Wiener filter for f at the current phi, and
  2. a BFGS line search on phi along the preconditioned mixed gradient (mixed_grad_phi_logpdf), with Hessian approximation pinv(Cphi^-1 + Nphi^-1).

The G mixing matrix is set to the identity (the MAP is invariant to it).

from cmb_lensing.simulate import load_sim
from cmb_lensing.map_joint import map_joint

data_set = load_sim(nside = 128, theta_pix = 2.5, pol = "I", master_seed = 67, uk_arcmin_t = 5)
field_predict, phi_predict = map_joint(data_set, num_steps = 30)

A full worked example, with plots of the lensing, inverse lensing, logpdf and the cross spectra of the reconstruction against the truth, can be found in the map_joint tutorial notebook.

docs.title: LCDM Sampling (sample_joint)
docs.text:
sample_joint (cmb_lensing/sample_lcdm.py) draws samples from the joint posterior \(P(f, \phi, \theta \mid d)\) by Gibbs sampling, where theta are the five LCDM parameters

PARAM_ORDER = ["theta_MC_100", "logA", "ns", "ombh2", "omch2"]

The optical depth to reionization tau is fixed at 0.05 and the neutrino mass mnu at 0.06. The fiducial values, the ±5-sigma search box and the parameter scales are GROUND_TRUTH, PARAM_BOUNDS and PARAM_SIGMA in cmb_lensing/constants.py.

docs.title: One Gibbs iteration
docs.text:
The structure mirrors CMBLensing.jl's sample_joint:

  1. f step (gibbs_sample_f): draw f from its conditional with a simulated realization plus a Wiener-filter correction.
  2. mix: change to the mixed parametrization \(f^\circ = L(\phi) \cdot D \cdot f\); \(\text{ }\phi^\circ = G \cdot\phi\) following Millea, et. al. 2020.
  3. phi step (gibbs_sample_phi): one HMC step on the mixed phi field with mass matrix given by \(G^{-2}(C_\phi^{-1} + N_\phi^{-1})\).
  4. theta step: for each sampled parameter, a Gaussian random-walk Metropolis move of width proposal_sigmas[name] on the mixed logpdf. Proposals outside param_ranges[name] or outside the CAMB grid are rejected.
  5. update \(C_\mathrm{\phi}\), \(C_f\), \(D\), \(G\) at the accepted theta.
  6. unmix back to (f, phi) with the updated D and G.

The theta step is skipped for the first num_burn_in_fix_theta iterations.

docs.title: Tuning
docs.text:
Before a large experiment, run a pilot chain by calling the __main__ method of sample_lcdm.py on a small map and tune

  • proposal_sigmas toward ~44 % acceptance per parameter,
  • hmc_step_size / hmc_num_steps toward ~65 % phi acceptance.

advanced_logging = {"phi_acceptance": True, "lcdm_acceptance": True, ...} prints the running rates. plot_log_pdf / plot_lcdm_sigmas write progress plots to cmb_lensing/sample_lcdm_output/, which must exist first.

See the sample_joint tutorial for a worked example, and LCDM Sampling on the HPC for running many chains in parallel.

docs.title: Outputs
docs.text: sample_joint returns param_vals, a dict of per-parameter lists. With hpc_path set, every iteration appends the latest value of every parameter to {hpc_path}{theta}_map_{map_idx}_chain_{sub_chain_idx}_history.txt, which chain_analysis.py reads and analyzes to form distributions out of the sampled data.

docs.title: The CAMB Grid
docs.text:
sample_joint needs the theory power spectra at every proposed LCDM parameter combination. It gets them from one of two precomputed sources of real CAMB spectra, selected by module-level switches in cmb_lensing/sample_lcdm.py (exactly one may be True):

Switch Source Size Use USE_CAMB_GRID = True (default) 5D tensor-product cubic spline over (H0, logA, ns, ombh2, omch2), camb_splines/camb_grid_spline.npz ~7.9 GB, downloaded on first use all five parameters; required for pol = "IP" / "P" USE_CAMB_SPLINE = True five 1D spline caches camb_splines/camb_<param>_grid.npz ~3 MB each, downloaded on first use one sampled parameter; temperature only

Both are fetched automatically from the Hugging Face dataset the first time they are needed (or all at once with cmb-lensing-download-splines, see Installation). To use your own grid instead, rebuild it on the cluster using the slurm scripts in /camb_grid_generation, SCP it back to your local machine and place it at camb_splines/camb_grid_spline.npz.

docs.title: Memory
docs.text: The grid is opened once per process and each spectrum's spline is built lazily on first use (~2.1 GB resident per spectrum). Temperature-only sampling loads TT + PP (~4.5 GB); pol = "IP" loads TT / EE / TE / PP (~9.1 GB).

docs.title: Validating the grid
docs.text:
python tests/test_camb_grid.py --grid camb_splines/camb_grid_spline.npz -n 20

compares the spline against direct CAMB at random interior points. Typical max |Δ ln Cl| is ~1e-3 (TT) to ~5e-3 (EE, near an acoustic trough).

docs.title: HPC Setup
docs.text: All cluster scripts are Slurm scripts. Before running any of them, create hpc_local.sh at the repository root as described in Installation.

docs.title: How the drivers work
docs.text:
Each pipeline folder has a driver that only submits jobs, and is run with bash, not sbatch:

bash get_lcdm_samples/sample_lcdm.sh

A driver can be run from any directory. It cds into its own folder, sources ../hpc_local.sh and sbatches its job script once per job. Job scripts find their Python file and hpc_local.sh through $SLURM_SUBMIT_DIR, and write their output inside the driver's folder, so the checkout can live anywhere.

The physical configuration (nside, theta_pix, noise_level, l_knee, ...) is set by editing variables at the top of each driver. Keep them the same across drivers for one experiment, so the chains, the phi-noise measurements and the forecasts all describe the same box.

Driver Output folder camb_grid_generation/camb_grid.sh camb_grid_generation/multi_param_CAMB_grid/ get_lcdm_samples/sample_lcdm.sh get_lcdm_samples/lcdm_sampler_data/<experiment>/ get_map_joint_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise.sh get_map_joint_phi_noise/map_joint_phi_noise_output/ get_sampler_phi_noise/get_sampler_phi_noise.sh get_sampler_phi_noise/sampler_phi_noise_output/ get_delensed_field_covariance/get_delensed_field_covariance.sh get_delensed_field_covariance/delensed_covariance_output/ runtime_comparison/run_performance_test.sh runtime_comparison/performance_results/

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
Clone the repository and install it in editable mode from the repository root (the folder holding pyproject.toml):

git clone https://github.com/zaneblood1/CMBLensing.py.git
cd CMBLensing.py
pip install -e .

This pulls in JAX (pinned to jax == jaxlib == 0.9.2), Flax, CAMB, NumPy, SciPy and Matplotlib. Python 3.10 or newer is required. JAX is configured for float64 globally on import.

Optional extras:

pip install -e ".[dev]"    #pytest + jupyter
pip install -e ".[docs]"   #MkDocs, to build this site locally

docs.title: Check the install
docs.text:
from cmb_lensing.simulate import load_sim
data_set = load_sim(nside = 64, theta_pix = 5, pol = "I", master_seed = 1)
print(f"Pixel resolution = {data_set.theta_pix} arcminutes per pixel")

If you wish to run the unit tests or actively contribute to the development of the repository it will also be necessary to have juliacall installed and a CMBLensing.jl checkout - see Testing for more information.

docs.title: Downloading the 5D CAMB grid
docs.text:
sample_joint evaluates its theory spectra by default through a 5D CAMB spline, camb_splines/camb_grid_spline.npz (~7.9 GB). This file and the five small 1D caches (camb_splines/camb_<param>_grid.npz) are too large to store on GitHub. They are hosted on the Hugging Face dataset zaneblood1/5D_LCDM_CAMB_Grid_Spline and are downloaded automatically into camb_splines/ the first time the code needs them (cmb_lensing/camb_splines.py). No manual step is needed.

To fetch all six files ahead of time, run

cmb-lensing-download-splines

On a cluster, run this once on a login node: compute nodes often have no internet access. You can also rebuild the grid yourself (Building the CAMB Grid) and place it at camb_splines/camb_grid_spline.npz. See The CAMB Grid for more information on how the two splines are used.

docs.title: HPC setup (hpc_local.sh)
docs.text:
If you wish to run any of the HPC slurm scripts for e.g. sampling LCDM parameters en masse or generating data for Fisher forecasting, you will need to make a copy of the hpc_local.example.sh script and fill it in with your own personal cluster configurations. The example script is gitignored to avoid sharing personal email accounts, etc.

cp hpc_local.example.sh hpc_local.sh

then edit hpc_local.sh:

#the conda install and environment the jobs run in
source /path/to/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh
conda activate myenv

#where Slurm mails job failures
export SBATCH_MAIL_USER=you@example.edu

#the CMBLensing.jl checkout, used only by runtime_comparison/
export CMBLENSING_JL_PATH=/path/to/CMBLensing.jl

Every driver and every job script it submits sources this file. See HPC setup for how the drivers work.

docs.title: Building these docs locally
docs.text:
mkdocs serve      #live-reloading preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000
mkdocs build      #static site in site/

docs.title: Building the CAMB Grid
docs.text: Most users should download the grid. Rebuild it when CAMB is upgraded or the grid's box changes.

docs.title: The 5D grid
docs.text:
The 5D spline is used to interpolate real CAMB spectra on a tensor-product grid over (H0, logA, ns, ombh2, omch2) with (tau = 0.05, mnu = 0.06, r = 0), evaluated in log spectra space (cmb_lensing/camb_grid_interp.py). The grid is laid out in H0 because a rectangular box in theta_MC_100 has corners CAMB cannot solve; the sampler works in theta_MC_100 and converts back and forth through a stored theta(H0, ombh2, omch2) table.

cd camb_grid_generation
bash camb_grid.sh                                            #875 jobs, one 81-point H0 sweep each
python merge_camb_grid.py --grid_dir multi_param_CAMB_grid   #-> multi_param_CAMB_grid/camb_grid_spline.npz
python ../tests/test_camb_grid.py --grid multi_param_CAMB_grid/camb_grid_spline.npz -n 20

Regenerating the grid on an cluster will result in 81 x 5 x 5 x 5 x 7 = 70_875 CAMB calls in total. The jobs need only numpy and CAMB. The merge splines one spectrum at a time, in ell chunks, so the tables are never all in memory. Move the result to camb_splines/camb_grid_spline.npz (a file already there is used as is, never re-downloaded). If the new grid should replace the shared one, upload it to the Hugging Face dataset and tell everyone to delete their local copy.

docs.title: The 1D caches
docs.text:
python camb_grid_generation/precompute_camb_1d.py <theta_MC_100|logA|ns|ombh2|omch2|all> [--test]

If you only wish to sample one parameter at a time, you can just create a single 1-D spline. Precomputed versions of these splines are hosted on the Hugging Face dataset with the 5D grid and downloaded on first use. The above code sweeps one parameter over PARAM_BOUNDS (50 nodes) with the others held at GROUND_TRUTH and writes camb_splines/camb_<param>_grid.npz. The shipped caches were made with CAMB 2.0.0.

docs.title: Chain Analysis
docs.text:
python get_lcdm_samples/chain_analysis.py

turns the chains into parameter distributions and compares them with every available Fisher forecast.

docs.title: What it computes
docs.text:
• The chains' covariance: one np.cov per map (its sub-chains concatenated), averaged over maps, with a delete-one-map jackknife error.
  • Per-parameter plots, each chain thinned by its integrated autocorrelation time.
  • Forecasts for each N_phi source, with the CAMB delensed T block and, where a file is given, the empirical one. Forecasts carry no error bars.
  • Phi-noise and delensed-spectra plots at the chains' noise level.

docs.title: Inputs
docs.text:
The measured inputs are arguments of main, set in __main__ for the run's noise level:

forecast_phi_noise = {"map_joint": "<merged map_joint_phi_noise.npz>",
                      "sample_joint": "<merged sampler_phi_noise.npz>"}
forecast_delensed_covariance = {"qe_delensed": "<merged delensed_covariance.npz>"}

A file-based N_phi source without an entry is skipped.

docs.title: Output Folder
docs.text: get_lcdm_samples/lcdm_chain_plots/noise_level_<noise>uk/

docs.title: Delensed Covariance
docs.text:
Measures the empirical per-mode covariance of the delensed temperature field, and its finite difference in theta, to replace the CAMB delensed T block of the Fisher forecast.

Each job uses one seed and runs at every stencil point \(\theta_0\) and \(\theta_0 \pm h_i\):

  1. load_sim(theta) (common random numbers: at one seed the fields differ only through the cosmology),
  2. inverse-lens the noiseless lensed field by the Wiener-filtered true phi \(W\phi\), with \(W = C_\phi / (C_\phi + N_\phi)\) built once at \(\theta_0\),
  3. store \(|F|^2 / n_\text{side}^2\) on the rfft grid.

The merge is the realization mean at each stencil point.

docs.title: Choosing N_phi for the Wiener Filter
docs.text:
Driver Setting What it Controls phi_noise="", qe_filter=lensed or delensed or unlensed, qe_response=unlensed or gradient the box quadratic estimator phi_noise=<path> the nphi of a merged map_joint or sampler phi-noise file

Match it to the forecast it will feed: nothing checks that the file's W was built from the same N_phi as the forecast's phi block.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
bash get_delensed_field_covariance/get_delensed_field_covariance.sh
#copy delensed_covariance_output/ to your machine, then
python get_delensed_field_covariance/merge_delensed_field_covariance.py --covariance_dir <delensed_covariance_output>

Other settings in the driver: derivative_params (the forecast's --params must be drawn from this list), step_sigma (0.05, in units of PARAM_SIGMA), num_realizations, seed_prefix. A 3-point job at nside 128 takes ~20 s.

docs.title: Output: delensed_covariance.npz
docs.text: delensed_fid, delensed_plus, delensed_minus and metadata.

docs.title: LCDM Sampling on the HPC
docs.text:
bash get_lcdm_samples/sample_lcdm.sh

submits run_single_lcdm_chain.sh once per (data map, chain). Specify num_maps data realizations and num_chains chains per map in the master slurm submission script sample_lcdm.sh. Averaging over maps removes the cosmic variance of any one map, and running several chains per map checks convergence.

docs.title: What to set in sample_lcdm.sh
docs.text:
Variables Meaning nside, theta_pix, noise_level, pol basic configurations like pixel resolution, map size, etc, *_ground the ground-truth cosmology the data are simulated at *_min, *_max the sampling range for each parameter (by default ±5 sigma) num_maps, num_chains, map_prefix how many realizations and chains; map seeds are map_prefix * map num_burn_in_fix_theta, iters_per_chain, hmc_num_steps, hmc_step_size sampler settings

Which parameters are sampled, and the proposal widths, are set in run_single_lcdm_chain.py. Tune them first with a pilot chain.

docs.title: Output
docs.text: Chains are written as *_history.txt files (one line per iteration, every parameter) under get_lcdm_samples/lcdm_sampler_data/<experiment>/. Copy that folder to your machine and run the chain analysis script.

docs.title: MAP Joint Phi Noise
docs.text:
Measures the per-mode reconstruction noise of map_joint at GROUND_TRUTH. Each job simulates one realization with load_sim, reconstructs phi with map_joint, and stores per rfft2 mode the moments of the estimate \(\hat\phi\) and the true phi:

\[ A = |\hat\phi|^2, \qquad B = \mathrm{Re}\, \hat\phi\, \phi^*, \qquad D = |\phi|^2 . \]

The merge averages them over realizations before taking the ratio

\[ r^2 = \frac{\langle B \rangle^2}{\langle A \rangle \langle D \rangle}, \qquad N_\phi = C_\phi \left( \frac{1}{r^2} - 1 \right), \]

with a delete-one-realization jackknife error.

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
bash get_map_joint_phi_noise/get_map_joint_phi_noise.sh          #one job per seed
#copy map_joint_phi_noise_output/ to your machine, then
python get_map_joint_phi_noise/merge_map_joint_phi_noise.py --noise_dir <map_joint_phi_noise_output>

Settings at the top of the driver: nside, theta_pix, noise_level, l_knee, map_joint_steps, num_realizations, seed_prefix.

docs.title: Output: map_joint_phi_noise.npz
docs.text:
Key Content nphi per-mode phi noise on the rfft2 grid; NaN where the mean cross is <= 0, 0 at the origin nphi_error jackknife error box / cosmology keys nside, theta_pix, noise_level, l_knee, param_names, params

Can be used in forecasting via fisher_forecast --nphi_source map_joint --phi_noise map_joint_phi_noise.npz or as the noise source for the delensed covariance.

docs.title: Sampler Phi Noise
docs.text:
Measures the phi reconstruction noise reached by the sampler's own posterior mean. One chain per realization samples (f, phi) | d with theta held at GROUND_TRUTH (sample_joint's Gibbs sweep minus the theta step, fixed_theta_chain.posterior_mixed_draws), started at phi = 0. Every phi sample is stored.

The merge burns each chain in, averages it into the posterior mean \(\bar\phi\), and forms the same per-mode estimator as the map_joint phi noise with \(\bar\phi\) in place of \(\hat\phi\).

docs.title: Running it
docs.text:
bash get_sampler_phi_noise/get_sampler_phi_noise.sh    #one chain per seed
cd get_sampler_phi_noise
sbatch merge_sampler_phi_noise.sh                      #set burn_in in it first

The merge works on running jobs: each chain flushes its samples every 10 sweeps to a memory-mapped sampler_phi_NNNN_samples.npy, and the merge reads only the sweeps its sidecar sampler_phi_NNNN.npz reports as done. A chain not yet past the burn-in is left out. Use rsync --sparse to copy a partial run.

Locally, for a small test:

python -m cmb_lensing.sampler_phi_noise --nside 64 --theta_pix 5 --n_maps 4 --n_sweeps 400 --burn_in 100 --out_dir <dir>

docs.title: Output: sampler_phi_noise.npz
docs.text: nphi (NaN where unmeasured, 0 at the origin), nphi_error, cphi, the mean moments, burn_in, n_used, the seeds and the box / cosmology keys. Can be used for forecasting via fisher_forecast --nphi_source sample_joint --phi_noise sampler_phi_noise.npz or as the phi_noise key in the delensed covariance slurm script.
